definition_english: Applying an existing rule, statutory provision, contractual clause, or administrative directive to a different subject, institution, or office while introducing only those adjustments in points of detail—such as names, titles, authorities, or procedural references—that are necessary to make it operative without altering its substantive essence.
definition_hindi: किसी विद्यमान नियम, सांविधिक उपबंध, संविदात्मक खंड या प्रशासनिक निदेश को किसी अन्य विषय, पद या संस्थागत संदर्भ पर इस प्रकार लागू करना कि उसके मूल स्वरूप को बदले बिना केवल नाम, पदनाम, प्राधिकारी या प्रक्रियात्मक ब्योरों में आवश्यक अनुकूलन कर लिए जाएँ।

etymology.english_origin: Unadapted borrowing from Late/Medieval Latin mūtātīs mūtandīs (British Latin 1272; English via Middle English c. 1525), an ablative absolute pairing perfect passive participle mūtātus ('having been changed') with gerundive of necessity mūtandus ('needing to be changed'), from Latin mūtāre ('to change').
etymology.pie_root: *mei- (1) ('to change, go, move'); Sanskrit cognate methati ('changes, alternates, joins, meets'), alongside Latin mūtuus and migrāre.
etymology.hindi_components: Sanskrit tatsama components: यथावश्यक (yathā + āvaśyaka, savarṇa-dīrgha sandhi), यथोचित (yathā + ucita, guṇa sandhi), आवश्यक, परिवर्तन, सहित. Reported in the research notes (not independently verified): in Hindi Shabdsagar Vol. 5 p. 555, यथोचित is headworded while यथावश्यक is absent from its alphabetical slot between यथावत् and यथावस्थित.

synonyms: with the necessary changes in points of detail
with such changes as are necessary
with the respective differences having been considered

morphology.slot_2: masculine a-stem noun परिवर्तन in oblique singular or oblique plural परिवर्तनों
morphology.slot_3: indeclinable simple postposition सहित (direct attachment without के) or compound postposition के साथ
morphology.sandhi: यथा + आवश्यक = यथावश्यक (savarṇa-dīrgha); यथा + उचित = यथोचित (guṇa)

syntactic_patterns: placed immediately before the target domain or predicate, often set off by commas

pronunciation.english_ipa: UK /m(j)uːˌtɑːtɪs muːˈtandɪs/; US /m(j)uˌtɑtəs m(j)uˈtɑndəs/, /mjuˌteɪtəs mjuˈtændəs/; Classical Latin [muːˈtaː.tiːs muːˈtan.diːs]

cultural_nuances: Indian government English releases occasionally append an inline plain-English gloss indicating lay opacity (e.g., MoD PIB release 2022)

Translated judicial texts may retain Devanagari transliteration alongside a Hindi gloss, though translated judgments can contain translation artifacts requiring verification against primary statutory texts
usage_restrictions: Avoid agentive यथोचित परिवर्तन करके with inanimate statutory subjects
Deprecate adjectival/gerundive यथोचित परिवर्त्य due to part-of-speech mismatch
Do not use unglossed Devanagari transliteration (म्यूटैटिस म्यूटैंडिस / मूटाटीस मूटान्डीस) as a standalone translation
Do not insert redundant के before सहित (*परिवर्तनों के सहित) or apply feminine pluralization (*परिवर्तनें)

linguistic_analysis.structural_shift: English borrows an unadapted two-word Latin ablative absolute functioning as an indeclinable adverb; Hindi expands it into a three-slot invariable manner-adverbial postpositional phrase (tatsama adjective + oblique masculine noun परिवर्तन + postposition सहित or के साथ).
linguistic_analysis.cstt_status: No exact Hindi entry could be verified directly on CSTT portals: cstt.education.gov.in was inaccessible and shabd.education.gov.in returned no extractable entry; CSTT's prefatory mandate is reported to exclude Law (विधि को छोड़कर) and the phrase is absent from the Parliamentary Work Glossary excerpt seen by the researcher.

conceptual_analysis.core_scope: Operative incorporation by reference permitting strictly necessary adaptations in points of detail while preserving the essential nature of the rule, as articulated by the Supreme Court of India in Ashok Service Centre v. State of Orissa (1983).
conceptual_analysis.contrastive_boundaries: Distinct from verbatim replication (यथावत्, permitting zero alteration) and from ceteris paribus (अन्य बातें समान रहने पर, holding background variables constant rather than adapting them).

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Identical conceptual restriction to strictly necessary adjustments (यथावश्यक).
pairwise_comparison.difference: Oblique plural परिवर्तनों mirrors Latin plural mutatis mutandis; unmarked oblique singular परिवर्तन is more compact in statutory clauses.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: High within legal prose; maintain uniform number within a document.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both express contextual adaptation of an existing rule or directive.
pairwise_comparison.difference: यथावश्यक restricts changes to what is strictly necessary; यथोचित denotes what is fitting or appropriate, widening interpretive latitude.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Interchangeable in banking and executive circulars; prefer यथावश्यक in primary legislation.

pairwise_comparison.difference: यथावश्यक adds the proportional limiter 'to the extent needed'; आवश्यक परिवर्तनों सहित is more transparent for non-specialist readers.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Interchangeable in administrative prose; prefer यथावश्यक in statutory drafting.

pairwise_comparison.difference: सहित is a compact Sanskrit indeclinable suited to dense gazette syntax; के साथ flows more naturally in explanatory and judicial prose.
सहित encodes an accompanying condition; करके encodes an agentive prior action that clashes with inanimate statutory subjects.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Not interchangeable in statutory or passive-regulatory sentences.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Share root elements यथोचित and परिवर्त-.
pairwise_comparison.difference: परिवर्त्य is an adjectival gerundive ('modifiable') lacking the completed-adaptation adverbial sense.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Refer to the same Latin legal expression.
pairwise_comparison.difference: Conceptual Hindi translation versus orthographically unstable, opaque Devanagari transliteration.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Not interchangeable outside metalinguistic legal quotation or glossing.
